facts.j3: J.3.5(1) — the number of bits in a byte (3.7)
facts.why: pos_seal memcpy's the 120-byte board into uint64_t w[15]; 120 bytes is 15 words only if a byte is 8 bits (sunfish.c L199-201)

facts.j3: J.3.14(1) — the values of the <limits.h>/<stdint.h> macros (5.2.5.3, 7.22).  J.3.6 has no entry for integer SIZES
facts.why: PACK_VM packs (uint32_t)(int) into the high half of a uint64_t and VM_VAL unpacks it; the move-ordering key is exact only at 32 bits (L649-652)
TABLE_SIZE and the node counters are long (L83, L496-497)
reached only through uint64_t, which <stdint.h> fixes exactly

facts.j3: J.3.8 (Arrays and pointers) — but its entries are about integer<->pointer conversion, which the corpus never does
facts.why: no integer<->pointer cast in the corpus (0 sites), so no observable depends on the width; the model needs it for sizeof only

facts.j3: NONE — C23 REMOVED it from J.3.  C17's integers list had five entries and C23's J.3.6 has four; the deleted sign-representation item is the auditable trace of the two's-complement mandate
facts.why: C23 6.2.6.2p6 NOTE 2 mandates it; the signed-overflow UB boundary the tier arms is stated against it.  This is the one place -std=c23 IS load-bearing for the value model: C17 permitted sign-magnitude and ones' complement too

facts.j3: J.3.5(5) — which of signed char / unsigned char has the same range, representation and behavior as plain char (6.2.5, 6.3.1.1)
facts.why: the board is char b[120] and CLS[(int)p->b[j]] indexes a 128-entry table by it (L346); every board byte is ASCII < 128, so no VALUE changes — but the in-bounds ARGUMENT is a function of the sign

facts.j3: NONE — this is DEFINED behavior (6.3.1.3p2), not implementation-defined.  Recorded as a fact so the wrap/refuse split stays checkable
facts.why: mix64's x *= 0xff51afd7ed558ccdULL is deliberate defined wraparound (L192-193); standard-guaranteed, recorded because the tier must NOT refuse it while refusing signed overflow

facts.j3: NONE — conversion TO an unsigned type is defined modulo (6.3.1.3p2), and has been since C89
facts.why: PACK_VM biases a signed val by (uint32_t)(val) ^ 0x80000000u (L649)

facts.j3: J.3.6(3) — the result of, or the signal raised by, converting an integer to a signed type when the value cannot be represented (6.3.1.3p3)
facts.why: VM_VAL converts the unbiased key back with (int)(... ^ 0x80000000u) (L652).  CORRECTED at M2 inch 2: this entry previously claimed C23 6.3.1.3 MANDATES the two's-complement result and that -std=c23 was load-bearing for it.  It does not.  N3220 6.3.1.3p3 is word-for-word identical to C11/C17 — 'either the result is implementation-defined or an implementation-defined signal is raised' — and J.3.6(3) still lists it.  So this is DEPENDED-ON IMPLEMENTATION-DEFINED behavior, which is exactly what this profile exists to pin, and the pin is the measurement below rather than a sentence in the standard

facts.j3: NONE — byte order is not in J.3; it is a consequence of the object-representation rules (6.2.6.1) that the standard leaves unspecified rather than implementation-defined
facts.why: pos_seal hashes the board THROUGH uint64_t words, so h is endian-dependent — but h is never observable: pos_eq uses it only as a fast reject in front of a full memcmp (L209-217) and the bucket layout it induces is unobservable by the file's own argument (L403-405).  Measured, deliberately NOT depended on

facts.j3: J.3.6(4) — 'the results of some bitwise operations on signed integers' (6.5.1), a catch-all that does NOT name shifts; the precise citation is normative 6.5.8p5
facts.why: the corpus has ZERO signed right shifts — all 6 >> sites are on uint64_t (L192-194, L652-653).  Measured so the claim stays checkable

facts.expr: _Alignof(int) == 4 && sizeof(struct { char c; int i; }) == 8 && _Alignof(struct { char c; int i; }) == 4 && sizeof(struct { char a; char b; }) == 2
facts.j3: J.3.9(1) -- the alignment requirements of structure and union members, and the padding between them (6.7.2.1). C23 leaves both implementation-defined; this profile pins the SysV/AAPCS shape both profiled hosts implement: every member at its own alignment, no reordering, the aggregate aligned to its widest member and its size rounded up to that alignment.
facts.why: torLayout computes struct/union size and member offsets from this rule (2026-08-25-c-26). C leaves the padding implementation-defined, so a layout computed from an UNDECLARED rule is a fabricated layout -- the same defect as a fabricated column, one abstraction up. Declared here so it is a profile decision like the scalar widths, and PROBED so it is checked on both hosts rather than assumed from one.

kind: abstract profile — a schema hosts satisfy, not one pinned machine
